professors.title: Professor of the Practice
professors.department_name: Political Science Department, Morrissey College of Arts and Sciences
professors.evidence_quote_or_summary: GPSP official contact page lists: 'Kathleen Bailey, Director, GPSP, Professor of the Practice, Political Science Department, kathleen.bailey@bc.edu'. The Political Science faculty directory confirms: 'Kathleen Bailey, Professor of the Practice, Director of the Gabelli Presidential Scholars Program'.

notes: The Gabelli Presidential Scholars Program is an undergraduate merit scholarship; its faculty leadership is the programme director Kathleen Bailey (Professor of the Practice, Political Science), who serves as the programme's principal faculty contact. Associate Director Jennie Thomas is programme staff (not faculty). Scholars are additionally matched with departmental faculty mentors in their areas of interest during their studies.

Harvard College's need-based financial aid for international students is administered by the Griffin Financial Aid Office (finaid.college.harvard.edu), an administrative office staffed by financial aid officers, not by supervising professors. This is an undergraduate need-based aid programme with no research supervision component, so no supervising professor exists to verify.

Princeton's need-based financial aid programme for international students is run by the Undergraduate Financial Aid and Student Employment Office within the Office of the Dean of the College (finaid.princeton.edu). Staff listed (Director Elizabeth Badger, Deputy Director Silvia Rodriguez, etc.) are administrative officers, not faculty. This undergraduate need-based grant aid programme has no supervising professors.

Brown's financial aid for international applicants is administered by the Office of Financial Aid (finaid.brown.edu) and the College's Financial Advising team (college.brown.edu), whose listed members are deans, advisors and counsellors (e.g., Sean Ferns, Dean of Financial Aid; Shannon DeLuca, Associate Dean for Financial Advising), not faculty. No supervising professor is tied to this need-based undergraduate aid programme.

Dartmouth's need-based aid for international students is administered by the Financial Aid office (financialaid.dartmouth.edu), led by Assistant Vice President and Executive Director G. Dino Koff and administrative staff. No supervising professors or faculty are attached to this undergraduate need-based aid programme.

The Aga Khan Foundation International Scholarship Programme is a private foundation scheme (akf.org/international-scholarship-programme) with no attached host institution: recipients must independently 'be admitted to a reputable postgraduate institution' of their own choosing, so there are no university professors tied to the scholarship. The 2026-2027 cycle is closed; the next cycle opens in early 2027.

professors.title: Associate Professor in Conflict Resolution; Head of Department
professors.department_name: Department of Peace Studies and International Development
professors.evidence_quote_or_summary: University of Bradford Rotary Peace Centre page lists: 'Dr Rhys Kelly (Head of Department)' among the Department of Peace Studies and International Development teaching staff who advise students on specialist research areas. His staff profile states: 'I am Associate Professor in Conflict Resolution and (since July 2024) Head of Department in the Department of Peace Studies and International Development.'

notes: The Rotary Peace Fellowship funds study at Rotary Peace Centers hosted by partner universities (rotary.org). Verified faculty leadership at two of the master's-degree Rotary Peace Centers: Uppsala University (Center Director Karen Brounéus) and the University of Bradford (Rotary Peace Centre Director Prathivadi Anand; Head of Department Rhys Kelly of the host Department of Peace Studies and International Development). Other centres (Duke/UNC, International Christian University, University of Queensland, Makerere, Bahçeşehir, Symbiosis) were not exhaustively researched due to the 3-professor limit.
